# smooth-corners

Squircle / continuous corners for the web, using the **exact geometry of Electron's `-electron-corner-smoothing`** (`shell/renderer/electron_smooth_round_rect.cc`). API modelled on [cornerKit](https://github.com/bejarcode/cornerKit). Vanilla JS core (4.8 KB gzip) + React bindings.

## Why another squircle lib?

cornerKit and figma-squircle use their own curve. This one ports Electron's C++ line-by-line, so the result is pixel-identical to an Electron app using `-electron-corner-smoothing`:

- Each corner = cubic bezier → circular arc → cubic bezier; edge consumed = `(1 + s) · r`.
- `s = 0` is exactly `border-radius`.
- Radii constrained like Blink's `FloatRoundedRect::ConstrainRadii` (so `9999` gives a capsule).
- Smoothing backs off **per edge** when corners collide: a capsule keeps smoothing on its long edges, short edges fall back to a true semicircle.
- The path always has the same command structure, so `clip-path` transitions interpolate.

## Vanilla

```js
import { SmoothCorners } from 'smooth-corners';

const sc = new SmoothCorners({ smoothing: 'system-ui' }); // 0.6 on macOS, 0 elsewhere
sc.apply('.card', { radius: 24, smoothing: 0.6 });
sc.apply('.btn', { radius: [12, 12, 4, 12], border: { width: 1, color: '#ddd', style: 'dashed' } });
sc.apply('.native');                // radius: 'css' -> use the element's own border-radius
sc.auto({ observe: true });         // [data-squircle] + dynamically inserted nodes
sc.update('.card', { radius: 32 });
sc.inspect(el);                     // effective radius / smoothing per corner, path, mode
sc.remove('.card');                 // restores original inline styles
sc.destroy();
```

```html
<div data-squircle data-squircle-radius="24" data-squircle-smoothing="60%"
     data-squircle-border-width="1" data-squircle-border-color="#ddd"></div>
<script src="dist/smooth-corners.iife.js"></script>
<script>new SmoothCorners().auto({ observe: true })</script>
```

## React

```jsx
import { Squircle, useSquircle } from 'smooth-corners/react';

<Squircle radius={20} smoothing="60%" className="card">…</Squircle>
<Squircle as="button" radius={9999}
  border={{ width: 1, gradient: [{ offset: 0, color: '#f97' }, { offset: 1, color: '#7af' }] }} />

const ref = useSquircle({ radius: 16 });
<img ref={ref} src="/me.jpg" />
```

## Path only (SSR, canvas, static SVG)

```js
import { smoothRoundRectPath, smoothRoundRectSVG } from 'smooth-corners/path';
smoothRoundRectPath(0, 0, 200, 60, 0.6, 9999);   // SVG `d`
new Path2D(smoothRoundRectPath(0, 0, w, h, 0.6, [24, 24, 8, 8]));
```

## Options

| option | type | default |
|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `number` · `[tl,tr,br,bl]` (CSS shorthand) · `{tl,tr,br,bl}` · `'css'` | `'css'` |
| `smoothing` | `0..1` · `'0%'..'100%'` · `'system-ui'` · `'none'` | `0.6` |
| `border` | `{ width, color, style: solid/dashed/dotted, gradient, angle }` | `null` |
| `precision` | decimal places in path data | `2` |

Elliptical radii collapse to `min(rx, ry)` — same as Electron's Blink patch. Without `clip-path: path()` support it falls back to plain `border-radius`.

## How it renders

`clip-path: path(...)` on the element itself (no wrapper), regenerated by one shared `ResizeObserver`; config kept in a `WeakMap`. Borders are an inert, `aria-hidden` SVG overlay stroked *inside* the shape along an inset squircle. Focus outlines are clipped by `clip-path` — use an inner focus ring (`box-shadow: inset …`) on clipped interactive elements.

## Dev

```
npm run build   # dist/ + demo/standalone.html
npm test        # geometry unit tests vs reference port + Playwright e2e
```

Geometry: Electron (MIT), after Figma's "Desperately seeking squircles".
